english.notes:
(i) This offence should be used for offences committed in England from 25th April 2024 due to changes in penalty made by section 20 of the Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023. For the document to be used before this date, see H19070.
(ii) For land in Wales, see H19071 due to different penalties for England and Wales.
(iii) Section 187A(2) of the Act provides that a local planning authority may, if any of the conditions is not complied with, serve a notice (referred to as a "breach of condition notice") on any person who is carrying out or has carried out the development or any person having control of the land, requiring him to secure compliance with such of the conditions as are specified in the notice.
(iv) Section 187A(10) of the Act provides that this offence may be charged by reference to any day or longer period of time and a person may be convicted of a second or subsequent offence under that subsection by reference to any period of time following the preceding conviction for such an offence.
(v) Section 187A(11) of the Act provided that it shall be a defence for a person charged with an offence under this section to prove that he took all reasonable measures to secure compliance with the conditions specified in the notice or where the notice was served on him by virtue of subsection 187A(2)(b), that he no longer had control of the land.
